correctness.rationale: For the centered regular-simplex Gram matrix, face-direction spaces intersect nontrivially exactly when their vertex sets share at least two vertices. Disjoint face-direction spaces are orthogonal. If two faces share exactly one vertex and have dimensions r and s, the Gram blocks are I+J and the cross block is all ones, so the largest normalized inner product is sqrt(r/(r+1))*sqrt(s/(s+1)). The source's trivial-intersection condition gives r+s<=n; strict monotonicity forces r+s=n and balancing gives r=floor(n/2), s=ceil(n/2). Substitution into the source's exact formula for M yields the displayed radius. An exact checker independently enumerates all face pairs through dimension 12.
